newsitem.title: USA: AT&T say consumer long-distance improves.
newsitem.headline: AT&T say consumer long-distance improves.

text.p: AT&T Corp on Wednesday said that its core consumer long-distance unit had gradually improved its performance and the proportion of customers switching between competitors -- known as churn -- was down.
"We have seen gradual improvement in this (fourth) quarter with revenues and volumes improving from the third quarter," said Richard Miller's AT&T's chief financial officer.

"While our consumer business is still not growing at the industry rate, we are making progress," he told a conference call. He said churn fell for the second straight quarter, as the unit focused on holding onto customers and cost control.
"The majority of One rate customers are existing AT&T customers moving from other calling plans and basic schedule rates. However, one rate has attracted a number of wins from competitors," he said.

Miller later told Reuters in an interview that the company had seen some easing in the pressure from small aggressive resellers and dial-around companies which had grabbed many customers in the middle of last year.

"It may be too early to claim victory, but we have our plans in place, and the consumer is now better informed," he said. Industry executives have long said many of these reseller services are not as cheap as they appear to be.
Miller said that the consumer business was still growing at slightly less than the industry rate in both revenues and volumes, though it is holding its own in market share among business customers.
Total wireline service revenues grew 3.2 percent for 1996, lagging volume growth of 5.9 percent.
Competitive pressures have produced overall lower revenue per minute across the industry as more users move to cut-price calling plans from paying the gradually increasing basic rates.
